title: AI‑Agentic Cloud Evolution 2026: AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Salesforce and Volcengine Drive Serverless, Sovereign and High‑Performance Shifts
core_insight: AI‑agent platforms and sovereign‑ready services across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, Salesforce and Volcengine are catalyzing a structural shift toward agentic, serverless, AI‑first and region‑controlled cloud architectures, while capital continues to flow into AI‑driven verticals.

dimension_texts.technology: AWS introduced Lambda Web Functions and ECS Gateway to simplify serverless HTTP workloads and container ingress, while Google Cloud launched an open AI‑native stack on Kubernetes enabling distributed inference and agent orchestration; simultaneously Azure rolled out Foundry Agent Service’s Copilot Harness and Azure Cloud HSM hardware audit logging, marking a decisive move toward agentic, serverless and AI‑first architectures across major clouds. AWS added Amazon S3 Tables for seamless Hive‑to‑Iceberg migration and Bedrock GPT‑6.1 Terra model; Google unveiled BigQuery Measures and ClusterNetworkPolicy experiments; Azure introduced Cobalt 200 VM for EDA workloads and a fault‑prediction system, further strengthening cloud‑native compute and security. Introducing Amazon ECS Gateway: A fully-managed ingress solution for ECS services Announcing AWS Lambda Web Functions AWS Continuum for code vulnerabilities is now generally available The open AI-native stack on Kubernetes: From open models to distributed inference and agents Introducing TPU Sync: Fast KV cache and weight transfer for inference and RL on TPU Experimenting with ClusterNetworkPolicy in GKE Building the next generation of multimodal AI experiences with fal in Microsoft Foundry Introducing the Microsoft Copilot harness in Foundry Agent Service Azure Cloud HSM Hardware Audit Logging: Verifiable audit trails for security and compliance
dimension_texts.infrastructure: No new pricing announcements from AWS, Google, or Azure, but Azure introduced sovereign‑ready regions and controls for regulated industries, while Volcengine launched its full suite of cloud products in China. AMD unveiled Zen 6 cores and revived EPYC X line plus Verano super‑chip, while Azure Cobalt 200 VM provides specialized EDA compute and Volcengine released ByteHouse high‑performance data warehouse, indicating a gradual uplift in high‑performance compute supply. AMD winds up Zen 6 cores for faster clock speeds
